requirement:
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.references.outline_selectors`. I derived the expected results from the requirement text and did not read implementation source.

- **Path from the root, with the empty selector selecting the root.**
  - `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` resolves nested paths such as `mod[local]/fn[run]` and `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`. Each resolved node's stored selector is asserted equal to the selector used to resolve it.
  - The same test asserts `resolve("")` returns node 0.
  - `parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments` asserts that `parse_selector("")` yields no segments.
  - `anonymous_container_selectors_use_identity_hashes_and_survive_descendant_edits` resolves `pair[items]/item@…/pair[f]`.
  - Malformed or empty segments such as `a//b`, `fn`, and `[run]` are rejected in `parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments`. A leading `/` is rejected in `outline_addresses_validate_selectors_without_reading_paths`.
- **Named segments `kind[name]`.** `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` covers about twenty node kinds. It asserts exact selector strings and that unknown or ambiguous selectors fail to resolve.
- **Anonymous segments `kind@hash`, with the first 12 hex digits of the identity hash.**
  - `anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes` checks the `use@` prefix and the 12-digit length. It checks that inserting a sibling leaves the existing selectors resolvable and that editing a node invalidates only that node's selector.
  - `anonymous_container_selectors_use_identity_hashes_and_survive_descendant_edits` asserts the selector equals `item@` plus `identity_hash[..12]`. It also asserts that the identity hash differs from the structural hash and that the selector survives a descendant edit.
  - The Markdown test asserts the `kind@` prefix and a 12-character hash for non-section nodes.
  - `parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments` shows hash parsing is case-normalised and round-trips.
- **`#N` disambiguation (one-based, in source order).**
  - `fn[repeated]#1` and `fn[repeated]#2` are asserted in `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry`. The un-numbered `fn[repeated]` is rejected, and unique siblings such as `fn[outer]` carry no suffix.
  - `anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes` asserts `#1` and `#2` for two identical `use` items.
  - `#0` is rejected in `parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments`.
- **`line` nodes are interchangeable.** `plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes` shows that two identical lines yield the same selector and that it resolves. It also checks that whitespace-only differences give the same selector and that `two words` and `twowords` differ.
- **Percent-encoding and reversibility.**
  - `names_round_trip_through_percent_encoding` asserts the exact encoding of space, `/`, `[`, `]`, `#`, `@`, `%`, tab, and multibyte and non-ASCII whitespace as UTF-8 bytes. It asserts that decoding restores the name and that raw reserved characters or bad escapes are rejected.
  - The end-to-end selector `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]/fn[edge]` appears in `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry`.
  - The error paths for malformed escapes and missing nodes are exercised in `profile_rules_map_only_matching_contexts_and_keep_other_nodes_transparent`.
  - Selector validation is exercised in `outline_addresses_validate_selectors_without_reading_paths`.
- **No line numbers in selectors.** Every asserted selector string omits line numbers. The inserted-lines scenario in `anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes` keeps the old selectors resolvable, which would fail if positions were embedded.

Obligations about how the hash is computed belong to `requirements.references.structural_hash`. Here it is only cited, so I did not reassess it. I found no unacknowledged gap and no marking gap.

text: :::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
